title: Helmet Usage Gap by Ride Type
dataSources: E-bike rides (`ebike:ride`), scooter trips (`scooter:trip`), skate sessions (`skate:session`), surf sessions (`surf:session`), snow runs (`snow:run`).
app: Micro-mobility and action-sport trackers — e-bike / e-scooter apps (VanMoof, Bosch eBike Flow), and skate / surf / snow session trackers (Trace, Slopes, Xensr) with IMU sensors — streamed to Splunk HEC via APIs and scripted inputs.
spl:
index=personal (sourcetype=ebike:ride OR sourcetype=scooter:trip)
| eval ride_type=if(sourcetype="ebike:ride","e-bike","e-scooter")
| stats count as trips, sum(eval(if(helmet_used="true",1,0))) as helmet_trips by ride_type
| eval helmet_pct=round(100*helmet_trips/trips,1)
| sort ride_type
description: Shows whether helmet use is slipping for one ride type more than another.
value: Safety habits often degrade first on the trips that feel shortest or most casual.
implementation: Log helmet-use flags on ride events in `index=personal`; compare usage percentage across ride types.
visualization: Two-bar comparison of helmet-use percentage by ride type.
grandmaExplanation: It records whether you are getting casual about helmets on one kind of ride more than another.
